source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Change all/random setting to non-default in this BIOS function.
3. Save and reboot.
4. Boot in to BIOS and  check your setting still exist.
5. Press load default,save and reboot.
6. Boot in to BIOS,setting in this function should match the SPEC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error log happen.
2. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
3. Check your setting still exist.
4. The default setting should matches SPEC."

original_test_intent: Verify that approved AMD CBS values persist across save/reboot and that Load Default restores silicon- and firmware-revision-specific SPEC values without CPU, memory-training, NUMA, thermal, power, boot or OS regressions.
original_method: Change fields on ADVANCE AMD CBS, save/reboot and verify persistence in BIOS; then Load Default, save/reboot and compare with SPEC while checking logs and normal reboot behavior.
manual_activity: A human must navigate AMD CBS, change each approved field, execute both save/reboot phases, select Load Default and inspect the values. Software monitoring can observe effects but cannot exercise the firmware menu.
required_inputs: Exact CPU family/stepping, board, BIOS and vendor firmware identity
Named CBS fields with baseline, safe non-default and SPEC-default values
CPU, DIMM, topology, device and health baseline
Console/operator, stable power and OOB/vendor recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random; approve every CBS field/value for the exact revision.
Exclude voltage, frequency, memory-training or other limit-changing controls unless explicitly reviewed with safety thresholds.
Do not exceed platform thermal or power envelopes or risk production data/workloads.
Stop on training loops, DIMM/NUMA/device loss, thermal/power alarms, hang, crash, boot or management loss.
Restore the approved final tuning profile.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only CPU, memory, NUMA, device, thermal, power, OS/BMC log and health evidence.
Compare BIOS captures and system topology against the approved matrix.
Do not drive BIOS, choose performance/security limits, launch stress without separate approval or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Obtain and approve the revision-correct CBS matrix, safety thresholds and recovery.
Perform/capture both firmware transition phases and any approved health observation.
Evaluate persistence/defaults and platform stability and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects agent execution of the pre-OS UI. No source command exists; OS/BMC telemetry is read-only supporting evidence and cannot replace firmware values.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the manual CBS sequence and add approved read-only CPU/memory/NUMA/thermal/power snapshots; do not use OS tuning utilities, model-specific registers or firmware-variable writes as substitutes.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source AMD sequence, no-script state and 5/20-minute fields are preserved; all/random remains preserved source wording but is not executable without a bounded matrix.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each approved CBS field, record exact platform revision, baseline, non-default, SPEC default, dependent CPU/memory/NUMA/power state and abort threshold; capture BIOS plus read-only health/topology through persistence, default restoration and final profile.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record CPU family/stepping, board revision, BIOS and vendor firmware identification, BMC, OS and telemetry versions; do not invent an AGESA value if the platform does not expose one.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor/platform CBS specification and safety/thermal/power limits for the exact revision.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds dependency and threshold controls and rejects arbitrary selection while preserving the two source phases.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction for the approved matrix; project exclusions and lack of undocumented fields are explicit.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Revision-correct CBS definitions, defaults, dependencies and recovery thresholds.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CBS menus are platform-specific and may expose coupled engineering controls; generic AMD guidance cannot establish supported values.

project_override_considerations: The project may choose a safe field subset and monitoring duration. Results apply only to that matrix and revision and must not be generalized to all CBS items or other CPU/board combinations.
expected_evidence: Platform/silicon/firmware identity, approval, baseline and recovery readiness
First save/reboot persistence plus CPU/memory/NUMA/thermal/power evidence
Load Default, second save/reboot, SPEC comparison and normal-boot evidence
Final tuning profile, topology, health/logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require non-default persistence and SPEC-default restoration. Their missing field and revision definitions are readiness gaps, not contradictory requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two-phase CBS purpose is clear. Exact values, dependencies and recovery are mandatory before execution but do not make the library definition permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees with manual classification and adds CBS-specific silicon, memory and power safety.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains revision matrix, health evidence and recovery controls while applying the V3.1 readiness distinction.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Limits claims to the approved platform matrix and separates agent telemetry from human firmware acceptance.

review_improvement: Prevents arbitrary CBS changes from causing memory-training or power/thermal failures and makes every accepted value traceable to the exact platform revision.
independent_technical_reasoning: The BIOS page interaction and visual persistence/default comparison are core acceptance steps and remain MANUAL ONLY. Automated telemetry is valuable but cannot prove the CBS UI control behavior.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat CBS changes, training/reboot or default load after any topology, thermal, power, boot or evidence anomaly; preserve first-failure data and obtain engineer disposition.
